Methods for nbreg objects

nbreg-methods.Rd

Standard extractor, summary, and prediction methods for negative binomial fits returned by nbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.nbreg'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  signif.stars = getOption("show.signif.stars"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson", "deviance"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("link", "response"), se.fit = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further arguments (currently ignored).

object, x

An object of class "nbreg" (or "summary.nbreg" for the print method of a summary).

signif.stars

Logical; show significance stars?

type

For residuals(): "response", "pearson", or "deviance". For predict(): "link" or "response".

newdata

Optional data frame in which to look for the covariates (and any offset variables). If omitted, the fitted values are used.

se.fit

Logical; if TRUE, predict() also returns standard errors (delta method on the response scale).

Value

coef(), fitted(), residuals() return numeric vectors; vcov() a matrix; logLik() an object of class "logLik"; nobs() an integer; predict() a vector, or with se.fit = TRUE a list with components fit and se.fit; summary() an object of class "summary.nbreg". The print methods return their argument invisibly.

Details

  • coef(), vcov(): estimated \(\beta\) and its covariance matrix \((X^\top\hat W X)^{-1}\) (with \(\theta\) treated as known).

  • logLik(): the maximized log-likelihood with attribute df = \(p + 1\) (the coefficients plus \(\theta\)), so stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() work.

  • fitted(): fitted means \(\hat\mu_i\).

  • residuals(): response residuals \(y_i - \hat\mu_i\), Pearson residuals \(\sqrt{a_i}(y_i - \hat\mu_i)/\sqrt{V(\hat\mu_i)}\) with \(V(\mu) = \mu + \mu^2/\theta\), or deviance residuals.

  • predict(): the linear predictor \(\hat\eta\) (type = "link") or the mean \(\hat\mu = e^{\hat\eta}\) (type = "response"), for the original data or for newdata, optionally with standard errors.

  • summary(): coefficient table with Wald z tests, plus \(\hat\theta\), its SE, the log-likelihood, AIC, and deviance.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 300
x <- rnorm(n)
y <- rnbinom(n, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.8 * x), size = 2)
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x)
#> 
#> Coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#> (Intercept)            x  
#>      0.4508       0.7669  
#> 
#> Theta: 1.95   Log-likelihood: -526.892 on 3 df
#> 
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -1.1939 -0.7791 -0.2593  0.4389  5.2098 
#> 
#> Coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  0.45081    0.06613   6.817 9.32e-12 ***
#> x            0.76687    0.06699  11.448  < 2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 1.95  (SE 0.3699)    Log(theta): 0.6678  (SE 0.1897) 
#> Log-likelihood: -526.892 on 3 df   AIC: 1059.78 
#> Residual deviance: 325.54 on 298 degrees of freedom
#> Outer iterations (IRLS + Newton-Raphson): 3 (converged) 
#> 
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.4508058   0.7668655 
vcov(fit)
#>              (Intercept)            x
#> (Intercept)  0.004373642 -0.001688731
#> x           -0.001688731  0.004487089
logLik(fit)
#> 'log Lik.' -526.8916 (df=3)
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 1059.783
head(residuals(fit, type = "pearson"))
#>          1          2          3          4          5          6 
#> -0.8050751  2.2472901 -0.7620322  1.2691926 -0.5032198  0.1494196 
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1)), type = "response")
#>        1        2        3 
#> 0.729016 1.569576 3.379309
